speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: asked the Minister for Manpower (a) why are employers required to pay the salaries of S Pass holders electronically but not for work permit holders; and (b) how does the Ministry verify that the amount stated in salary vouchers tally with the cash amount paid to workers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: To further encourage the adoption of e-payment of worker salaries, MOM introduced an online facility in 2014 to facilitate employers opening bank accounts for their work permit holders when applying for their work permits.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: In addition, MOM also mandated the issuance of itemised payslips and written key employment terms since April 2016.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Workers should ensure that they are paid the amount stated in their salary vouchers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: And when there is any discrepancy, workers should seek clarifications from their employer and not sign on the salary vouchers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: If workers are not able to resolve such disputes with their employers, they should seek help from MOM immediately.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Anyone who has information on employers who do this should report this to MOM and action would be taken against the errant employers.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can I just check with the Minister of State whether MOM does track the number of employers that open a bank account for their work permit holders when they apply for their work permits?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: And two, does MOM know what proportion of work permit holders currently have bank accounts here in Singapore?

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: From our statistics, as regard the provisions of the online e-payment during the application process for the work permit, close to two-thirds of the employers have actually chosen to open e-payment accounts for their employees.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: If I could ask if MOM is willing to incentivise the process so as to try to incentivise the employers when they apply for the work permit to apply also for the bank accounts for their work permit holders.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: But, as mentioned in my reply, not all the permit holders actually prefer to receive their salary electronically for a range of reasons.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: And also, not all the employers are able to do this because of administrative fees and other constraints.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: So, I think we should provide a framework where those who need e-payment of their salary will be able to do so and, at the same time, to also allow for some flexibilities for those who are genuinely not able to adopt this payment method, so that there will be flexibility and also convenience between the employers and employees.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: When we continue to do our policy review, we will find ways and means to further encourage our employers to adopt this e-payment method.
